column1: # Katagiri morph -> lexeme accuracy set (task A4c). 200 labelled UniDic morphs.
# Columns, tab-separated: lemma  reading  pos1  expected_jmdict_seq  note
#   lemma   UniDic's lemma field, verbatim - including the -disambiguator suffix
#           it appends to homograph lemmas (私-代名詞, コーヒー-coffee), which
#   reading UniDic's lemma reading (lForm), katakana. Empty when UniDic gave none
#   pos1    UniDic's coarsest part of speech.
#           The JMdict ent_seq a human would point at, or EMPTY when the correct
#           answer is "no map" - punctuation and compounds JMdict does not list.
#           Every seq here was looked up in a real import of
#           against that entry's written forms, readings and glosses. None are
#           invented, and none were taken on trust from the matcher's own output.
#   note    "<category>: <comment>". The category is machine-read by the accuracy
#           harness to report a per-category breakdown; the comment says why the
#           row is interesting, and flags the rows whose lemma spelling was added
#           by hand rather than observed from the tokenizer.
# Matching is entry-level: a morph identifies a JMdict entry, not one of its
# senses, so nothing here labels a sense_idx. See katagiri.normalizer.
# Rows whose lemma is marked "hand-added" are spellings the vendored UniDic does
# not itself produce. They are real Japanese orthography and are here to exercise
# the okurigana rung, which natural UniDic output almost never reaches because
# JMdict already lists UniDic's preferred spelling as a variant.
